mn125:7.3: Remember, kāma refers to the objects of sense-pleasure as well as to the interior desire.
mn125:14.5: ‘Not easy … as a polished shell’ refers to the difficulty of living the holy life as utterly perfect and pure while remaining a householder.
mn125:15.2: Pātimokkha: the name for the code of 227 rules fundamental to the bhikkhu life, recited on Full and New Moon days in the presence of all bhikkhus resident in a monastery.
mn125:24.5: ‘Thoughts’ here and ‘initial application’ elsewhere are both translations of vitakka; thought is too gross a word to use in connection with jhāna, so uniformity of rendering must be sacrificed.
mn125:31.6: A bhikkhu is an elder (thera) after ten years in the Sangha, a middle bhikkhu after five years, a new bhikkhu under five years.
